claims.description: A bomb made of a self-sustaining radioactive element that keeps exploding continuously once triggered by admitting air is imagined.

claims.quote: The bomb flashed blinding scarlet in mid-air, and fell, a descending column of blaze eddying spirally in the midst of a whirlwind.
claims.description: A single atomic bomb dropped from an aeroplane produces a continuous fiery explosion over a city.

claims.quote: What the earlier twentieth-century chemists called its half period was seventeen days; that is to say, it poured out half of the huge store of energy in its great molecules in the space of seventeen days
claims.description: The imagined element loses half its radioactive energy roughly every seventeen days.

claims.quote: to this day the battle-fields and bomb fields of that frantic time in human history are sprinkled with radiant matter, and so centres of inconvenient rays.
claims.description: Battlefields hit by atomic bombs remain radioactive for generations afterward.

claims.quote: Before the last war began it was a matter of common knowledge that a man could carry about in a handbag an amount of latent energy sufficient to wreck half a city.
claims.description: A single person could carry a portable explosive powerful enough to destroy half a city.

claims.quote: the swift aeroplane, with its atomic engine as noiseless as a dancing sunbeam and its phosphorescent gyroscopic compass, flew like an arrow to the heart of the Central European hosts.
claims.description: An aeroplane powered by an atomic engine and guided by a glowing gyroscopic compass is imagined.

claims.quote: Collective civilisation, the ‘Modern State,’ was still in the womb of the future
claims.description: Large collective states organized around modern citizenship are imagined as a coming development.

claims.description: A base of flying machines from which to bomb German industrial centers is imagined as part of a war plan.
